2609.04877.title: MARLA: A Conceptual Scaffold for Regulatory Learning under the EU AI Act
2609.04877.paper_summary: The EU AI Act positions regulation as part of the infrastructure for safe, trustworthy and market-ready innovation. Realising this ambition requires regulatory learning: the evidence generated during implementation must be translated into governance and legal knowledge that supports consistent interpretation, effective oversight, and adaptation as technologies evolve. Yet the actors who produce this evidence and those who rely on it operate in different professional worlds. This paper proposes MARLA (Map, Assess, Report, Learn, Adapt), a conceptual scaffold organising regulatory learning as a five-stage cycle centred on the implementation of legal requirements into socio-technical practices, situated at the Local, National and European levels of the AI Act's governance architecture. Deliberately non-prescriptive, MARLA gives technical and legal stakeholders a shared vocabulary in which each of the first three stages generates its own documentable form of regulatory learning. We illustrate the scaffold with two piloted case studies and a prospective National-to-European illustration.
2609.04877.paper_summary_zh: 歐盟人工智慧法案將監管視為安全、值得信賴且市場準備就緒的創新基礎設施的一部分。實現這一目標需要監管學習：在實施過程中產生的證據必須轉化為支持一致解釋、有效監督和隨著技術演變而調整的治理和法律知識。然而，產生這些證據的行為者與依賴這些證據的行為者卻在不同的專業領域中運作。本文提出了MARLA（地圖、評估、報告、學習、適應），這是一個概念性框架，將監管學習組織為一個五階段循環，重點放在法律要求的實施與社會技術實踐的結合，並位於人工智慧法案治理架構的地方、國家和歐洲層面。MARLA故意不具指導性，為技術和法律利益相關者提供了一個共享的詞彙，其中前三個階段各自生成其可文檔化的監管學習形式。我們用兩個試點案例研究和一個前瞻性的國家到歐洲的示例來說明這個框架。
